title: Lattice Theta Functions with Half-Integral Characteristics
description:
Exact proofs, certificates, and reproducible computations for identical vanishing of lattice theta functions with half-integral characteristics.

The symmetry converse holds in ranks one through three and fails in rank four. Versions 1.1.0 and 1.1.1 add the rank-four follow-up results: an identically vanishing even characteristic of a lattice of determinant 1729 whose two coset lattices are the Conway–Sloane isospectral pair L-(1,7,13,19), L+(1,7,13,19), which are not isometric (eight such configurations are certified); a counterexample to the symmetry converse of determinant 1156 with automorphism group {I, −I}, the same Eisenstein-integer construction as the original determinant-23,716 example; and the rank-four parity property, which fails for indecomposable odd lattices with determinant not divisible by four first at determinant 49 and for even indecomposable lattices of odd determinant first at determinant 121 (a Gaussian-integer structure), with complete class lists and structural theorems. Two further deductions from an independent assessment are included: the ordinary theta series does not determine the parity property in rank four, and a determinant-3844 isospectral non-isometric pair is proved at every level by weight-two Sturm bounds.

Version 1.1.1 adds a correction: halving the even determinant-4480 level-four lattice gives an odd lattice of determinant 280 with automorphism group {I, −I} and a level-four zero. It is the smallest known level-four zero and the smallest known counterexample to the symmetry converse, so the bracket for the minimum counterexample determinant is 24 < det ≤ 280 (no minimality claim; version 1.1.0 stated 24 < det ≤ 1156).

The release also includes the low-rank parity classification, the classification of irreducible crystallographic root lattices in the stated normalization, exact determinant-at-most-24 censuses through rank four, and a checked literature note on the isospectrality sources. No literature-priority claim is made.

Reproduction uses Python 3.11 or later and the Python standard library only. The included reviews are AI-assisted local mathematical reviews with independent computational replication. They are not a claim of journal publication or formal peer review.
